examples.ko: 용광로에서 쇠가 녹아서 빨간 물처럼 흘러요.
examples.en: Iron melts in the blast furnace and flows like red water.

examples.ko: 제철소에 가면 커다란 용광로를 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you go to a steel mill, you can see a huge blast furnace.

examples.ko: 용광로 안은 온도가 천 도가 넘어요.
examples.en: The temperature inside the blast furnace is over a thousand degrees.
The classroom is as hot as a furnace today.

examples.ko: 이 도시는 여러 문화가 섞인 용광로예요.
examples.en: This city is a melting pot where many cultures mix.

examples.ko: 용광로 앞에서 일하는 사람들은 특별한 옷을 입어요.
examples.en: People who work in front of the furnace wear special clothes.

explain: '용광로처럼 덥다'처럼 아주 뜨거운 곳을 비유할 때 써요. '문화의 용광로'처럼 여러 사람과 문화가 한곳에 섞여 있는 곳을 말할 때도 많이 써요. 영어의 'melting pot'과 비슷해요.
explain_en: It is used as a metaphor for a very hot place, as in '용광로처럼 덥다'. It also appears in '문화의 용광로' for a place where many people and cultures mix, similar to the English 'melting pot'.

examples.en: My friend cheered me on, so I got a big boost of courage.
Hearing the teacher's praise gave me courage, so I gave my presentation.
The players are filled with courage by the fans' applause.
When my family is next to me, I automatically feel brave.
The child, full of courage, went on the errand alone.

examples.ko: 엄마 말씀을 듣고 용기백배한 얼굴로 시험장에 들어갔어요.
examples.en: After hearing my mom's words, I went into the exam room looking full of courage.

explain: 보통 말할 때는 '용기가 나다', '힘이 나다'라고 해요. '용기백배'는 응원이나 칭찬을 받고 힘이 확 솟을 때 쓰고, 글이나 기사에서 더 자주 보여요. '용기백배해서', '용기백배한 얼굴'처럼 이어서 써요.
explain_en: In everyday talk people usually say '용기가 나다' or '힘이 나다'. '용기백배' is used when cheering or praise suddenly gives you strength, and it shows up more in writing and news. It is typically used as '용기백배해서' or '용기백배한 얼굴'.

examples.en: It started out grand, but it ended in an anticlimax.

examples.ko: 이번 계획도 용두사미가 될까 봐 걱정돼요.
examples.en: I'm worried this plan will also fizzle out.

examples.ko: 그 드라마는 마지막 회가 용두사미라서 실망했어요.
examples.en: The last episode of that drama was an anticlimax, so I was disappointed.
Everyone felt sorry about the anticlimactic ending.
My exercise plan fizzles out every time.
The construction that began with big promises just petered out.

explain: 시작은 대단했는데 끝이 흐지부지할 때 써요. 처음부터 끝까지 잘 마무리했다는 뜻의 '유종의 미'와 반대되는 느낌이에요. '용두사미로 끝나다', '용두사미가 되다'로 많이 말해요.
explain_en: Use it when something starts impressively but ends weakly. It feels like the opposite of '유종의 미' (a fine finish). It is often used as '용두사미로 끝나다' or '용두사미가 되다'.

examples.en: The child said he wanted to go to the toilet.
We stopped the bus and relieved ourselves for a moment.
The puppy does its business in the designated spot.
I needed the toilet badly, so I ran to the restroom.
I always wash my hands after using the toilet.
When do you start potty training a baby?

explain: '용변을 보다'로 쓰고, 화장실 가는 일을 직접 말하지 않고 점잖게 돌려 말하는 표현이에요. 아기나 반려동물 이야기, 안내문에서 자주 나와요. 친구끼리는 보통 '화장실 가다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used as '용변을 보다', a polite, indirect way to talk about going to the toilet. It often appears in talk about babies and pets and on signs. Among friends people usually just say '화장실 가다'.

examples.en: Strength surges up in my chest.
Hot water gushed up from underground.
Joy welled up at the news of the victory.
Spring water gushes out from between the rocks.
Starting a new job makes my motivation surge.
Anger surged up so much that I couldn't speak.

explain: 물이 솟는 모습뿐 아니라 힘, 기쁨, 의욕 같은 마음이 크게 솟아오를 때도 많이 써요. '솟구치다'와 비슷하게 쓸 수 있지만 '용솟음치다'가 조금 더 글에서 자주 보여요. 활용은 '용솟음쳐요', '용솟음쳤어요'예요.
explain_en: It describes not only water spurting up but also strong feelings such as strength, joy or motivation surging. It is close to '솟구치다' but appears a bit more in writing. It conjugates as '용솟음쳐요' and '용솟음쳤어요'.

examples.en: The baby strained so hard that its face turned red.

examples.ko: 아무리 용써도 이 뚜껑은 안 열려요.
examples.en: No matter how hard I strain, this lid won't open.
Don't strain yourself, I'll help you.
He keeps struggling hard to come in first.
I strained to lift the heavy load.
Straining won't do any good in this matter.

explain: 온 힘을 모아 낑낑대는 모습이에요. '용써도 안 된다', '용써 봐야 소용없다'처럼 안 되는 상황에서 많이 말해요. '애쓰다'보다 힘을 꽉 주는 느낌이 강해요. '쓰다'처럼 '용써요'로 활용해요.
explain_en: It describes putting all your strength into something and grunting with effort. It often appears in cases that don't work out, like '용써도 안 된다' or '용써 봐야 소용없다'. It feels more physical than '애쓰다'. It conjugates like '쓰다': '용써요'.

examples.en: That person handles work very carefully.
I prepared thoroughly, so there were no mistakes.
I made a careful plan before the trip.
My older sister is rather meticulous by nature.
Thanks to my well-prepared friend, we had an umbrella.

examples.ko: 너무 용의주도해서 좀 답답할 때도 있어요.
examples.en: He is so thorough that it can feel stifling sometimes.

explain: 빈틈없이 미리 준비하고 조심하는 사람이나 계획에 써요. 보통은 칭찬이지만 계산적인 느낌을 줄 때도 있어요. '용의주도하게 + 동사', '용의주도한 사람'으로 많이 써요.
explain_en: It describes a person or plan that is carefully prepared in advance with no gaps. It is usually praise, but it can sometimes sound calculating. It is commonly used as '용의주도하게 + verb' or '용의주도한 사람'.

examples.en: My father is a welder who works at a shipyard.
The welder joins steel plates, sparks flying.
You need a certificate to become a welder.
My uncle is a welder with twenty years of experience.

examples.ko: 용접공은 보호 안경을 꼭 써야 해요.
examples.en: Welders must wear protective goggles.

examples.ko: 현장에서 용접공 두 명이 일하고 있어요.
examples.en: Two welders are working at the site.

explain: 직업을 말할 때는 '용접공이에요'라고도 하고 '용접 일을 해요'라고도 해요. 기술 직업 이름에 붙는 '-공'은 기술자를 나타내요. 현장 이야기나 구인 공고에서 많이 보여요.
explain_en: To say the job you can say '용접공이에요' or '용접 일을 해요'. The '-공' ending marks a skilled worker. You often see it in talk about work sites and in job ads.

examples.en: The president decided to step down for the sake of his juniors.
Fans were surprised by the news of the manager's resignation.
He announced that he would withdraw from politics.
He stepped aside to open the way for the younger ones.
Calls for the chairman to step down are growing.
It was praised as a graceful withdrawal.

explain: 높은 자리에 있던 사람이 후배를 위해 스스로 물러날 때 쓰는 말이라 뉴스와 기사에서 보여요. 쫓겨났을 때는 쓰지 않고 '해임'이라고 해요. 그냥 그만두는 '사퇴'보다 스스로 결심했다는 느낌이 더 강해요.
explain_en: It is used when someone in a high position steps aside of their own will for those who come after, and appears in news. It isn't used when someone is forced out; that is '해임'. Compared with '사퇴', it stresses that the person decided it themselves.

examples.en: The ugeojiguk my mom cooked tastes really rich and savory.
On cold days I think of ugeojiguk.
Shall I put a little more soybean paste in the ugeojiguk?
I ordered the ugeojiguk set meal at the restaurant.
Ugeojiguk is delicious with rice mixed into it.
Every winter my grandmother cooked ugeojiguk for us.

explain: 우거지는 배추나 무의 겉잎을 말해요. 그 우거지를 넣고 된장을 풀어 끓이는 집이 많아요. 발음은 [우거지꾹] 또는 [우거짇꾹]이에요.
explain_en: 우거지 refers to the outer leaves of cabbage or radish, and many households cook the soup with soybean paste. It is pronounced [우거지꾹] or [우거짇꾹].

examples.en: He tried to force the door open.
If you force a child, he dislikes it even more.
You should talk it out; forcing things is not okay.
I crammed all my clothes into the bag by force.

examples.ko: 회의에서 우격다짐 식으로 결정하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You can't make decisions in a meeting by pushing them through.
I couldn't resist the pressure and ended up going along.

explain: 말이 통하지 않을 때 힘이나 기세로 억지로 밀어붙이는 느낌이에요. 사람에게 억지로 시킬 때도, 물건을 억지로 밀어 넣을 때도 써요. '우격다짐으로 하다', '우격다짐으로 밀어붙이다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It carries the feel of pushing something through by force or sheer pressure when reasoning doesn't work. It is used both for forcing people and for cramming things in. People say '우격다짐으로 하다' or '우격다짐으로 밀어붙이다'.

examples.ko: 일부 나라에서 정치의 우경화가 나타났다는 기사를 읽었어요.
examples.en: I read an article saying that politics in some countries has shifted to the right.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 사회의 우경화를 다룬 기사를 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw a news article about the rightward shift of society.

examples.ko: 우경화 흐름을 주제로 한 토론회가 열렸어요.
examples.en: A forum on the rightward trend was held.
The professor explained the causes of the rightward shift.
An analysis said the rightward shift is speeding up.

examples.ko: 선거 결과를 우경화라고 평가하는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people describe the election result as a rightward shift.

explain: 정치나 사회, 정당이 오른쪽으로 기울어지는 것을 말하며 뉴스와 사회 수업에서 나와요. 반대로 왼쪽으로 기우는 것은 '좌경화'라고 해요. '우경화 현상', '우경화 경향'으로도 자주 써요.
explain_en: It refers to politics, society or a party moving toward the right, and appears in news and social studies. Moving the other way is '좌경화'. It is also common in '우경화 현상' and '우경화 경향'.

en: turn rightist; turn to the political right side

examples.ko: 그 나라는 해마다 점점 우경화하고 있어요.
examples.en: That country is shifting further right every year.
There was criticism that the government is turning to the right.
They say that if society shifts to the right, policies change too.
That party moved to the right, and its supporters left.
Some people say the media has turned rightist.
I watched a documentary about the rightward-moving mood.

explain: 주로 정부, 정당, 사회, 언론 같은 집단이 주어로 나오고 뉴스 말투예요. 반대는 '좌경화하다'예요. 일상 대화에서는 '오른쪽으로 기울다'라고 풀어서 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It mostly takes groups such as governments, parties, society or media as the subject, and has a news-like tone. The opposite is '좌경화하다'. In casual talk people may spell it out as '오른쪽으로 기울다'.

examples.en: The market is swarming with people.
Tadpoles were swarming in the pond.
Bugs are swarming on the rotten fruit.
The beach is crawling with tourists on the weekend.
I was shocked because rats were swarming in the storeroom.
I want to avoid places teeming with people.

explain: 작은 것이나 사람이 좁은 곳에 많이 모여 움직일 때 써요. '북적거리다'가 활기찬 느낌이라면 '우글거리다'는 조금 답답하거나 지저분하다는 느낌이 있어요. 벌레, 쥐, 올챙이 같은 것에도 자주 써요.
explain_en: It is used when many small things or people move around together in a tight space. While '북적거리다' feels lively, '우글거리다' can feel stuffy or unpleasant. It is often used for bugs, rats and tadpoles.

examples.ko: 나무 밑에 개미가 우글우글 모여 있어요.
examples.en: Ants are gathered in swarms under the tree.

examples.ko: 휴가철 공항에 사람들이 우글우글 몰려 있어요.
examples.en: People are crowded together at the airport in the holiday season.
The fish in the tank are swarming around.

examples.ko: 쓰레기통 주변에 벌레가 우글우글 있어서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was startled because bugs were swarming around the trash can.
Kids gathered in crowds at the amusement park.

examples.ko: 우글우글 모여 있는 비둘기를 피해서 걸었어요.
examples.en: I walked around the pigeons flocked together.

explain: '우글우글 + 모이다/몰리다/있다'처럼 쓰고, 우글거리는 모양을 나타내요. 사람이 많을 때는 '바글바글'도 비슷하게 자주 말해요. 벌레나 동물이 모여 있는 모습에도 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It is used like '우글우글 + 모이다/몰리다/있다' to show the swarming look. For lots of people, '바글바글' is also often used in a similar way. It suits scenes of bugs or animals huddled together.

en: with a clatter; with a thump

examples.en: The child tumbled down the stairs with a clatter.
There was a thumping noise from upstairs.
The shelf collapsed and everything crashed down.
My younger sibling came running in with a thump.
The things on the desk fell with a clatter.

examples.ko: 우당탕 하는 소리에 놀라서 나가 봤어요.
examples.en: The loud crash startled me, so I went out to look.

explain: 물건이 요란하게 부딪치거나 사람이 넘어지고 뛰는 소리를 나타내요. 한 번 '쿵' 하는 소리와 달리 여러 소리가 이어져 시끄러운 느낌이에요. '우당탕 소리가 나다', '우당탕 넘어지다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It imitates the loud sound of things crashing or someone tumbling or running. Unlike a single '쿵', it suggests several noises in a row and a noisy scene. It is used as '우당탕 소리가 나다' or '우당탕 넘어지다'.

examples.en: When I turned my neck, it made a cracking sound.
Hail rattled down on the roof.
The dry branches snapped with a crack.
I crunched through the nuts.
Big raindrops started pattering down.

examples.ko: 기지개를 켜자 뼈마디에서 우두둑 소리가 났어요.
examples.en: When I stretched, my joints made a cracking sound.

explain: 단단한 것이 부러지거나 뼈마디가 꺾이거나 굵은 빗방울이나 우박이 떨어질 때 나는 소리예요. 소리가 계속될 때는 '우두둑우두둑'이라고 해요. 한 번 부러지는 소리는 '뚝'이 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It imitates the sound of something hard snapping, joints cracking, or big raindrops or hail falling. A continued sound is '우두둑우두둑'. For a single snap, '뚝' is more natural.

examples.en: I'm slow-witted, so I take a while to understand.

examples.ko: 그는 우둔해 보여도 사실은 눈치가 빨라요.
examples.en: He may look dull, but he actually catches on quickly.
You shouldn't tease someone for being dull.

examples.ko: 곰은 우둔한 동물처럼 보이지만 아주 영리해요.
examples.en: Bears look like dull animals, but they are very clever.
I missed the chance because I was so thickheaded.

examples.ko: 그렇게 우둔하게 굴지 말고 잘 생각해 보세요.
examples.en: Don't act so dull; think it over carefully.

explain: 머리가 잘 안 돌고 반응이 느리다는 뜻이라 다른 사람에게 쓰면 심한 말이에요. 자기를 낮출 때나 글에서 더 자연스러워요. '멍청하다'는 더 거친 말이고, '어리석다'는 판단이 잘못된 점을 말해요.
explain_en: It means slow in thinking and reacting, so it is harsh when said about another person. It is more natural for putting yourself down or in writing. '멍청하다' is even ruder, and '어리석다' focuses on poor judgment.

examples.ko: 우락부락 밀치고 들어오는 사람 때문에 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was startled by a person who shoved his way in roughly.

examples.ko: 우락부락 성을 내는 모습에 아이가 놀랐어요.
examples.en: The child was startled by the rough way he lost his temper.
Please don't speak so harshly.
I ran away when I saw the dog fiercely rushing at me.

examples.ko: 우락부락 인상을 쓰고 있어서 말 걸기 무서웠어요.
examples.en: He was scowling fiercely, so I was afraid to talk to him.

examples.ko: 우락부락 소리치던 아저씨가 곧 미안하다고 했어요.
examples.en: The man who had been shouting roughly soon said he was sorry.

explain: 말이나 행동이 거칠고 사나운 모양을 꾸며 줘요. 생김새나 체격을 말할 때는 보통 '우락부락하다'를 써요. '우락부락 + 성을 내다/소리치다'처럼 거친 행동과 함께 써요.
explain_en: It describes speech or behavior that is rough and fierce. For looks or build, people normally use '우락부락하다'. It pairs with rough actions, as in '우락부락 성을 내다' or '우락부락 소리치다'.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 얼굴이 우락부락해서 처음엔 무서웠어요.
examples.en: His face looked so tough that I was scared at first.

examples.ko: 우락부락한 팔뚝의 아저씨가 짐을 들어 줬어요.
examples.en: A man with thick, rough-looking arms carried my bags.
He looks tough, but he likes puppies.
My older brother worked out and his body became beefy.
The tough-looking guard greeted me first.
His voice is rough too, so the children are afraid of him.

explain: 생김새나 체격이 거칠고 억세 보일 때 써요. 외모를 평가하는 말이라 앞에서 직접 말하면 실례일 수 있어요. '우락부락하게 생겼지만 착하다'처럼 겉모습과 다르다고 말할 때 자주 써요.
explain_en: It describes a face or build that looks rough and tough. Since it comments on appearance, saying it to someone's face can be rude. It is often used to contrast looks with personality, as in '우락부락하게 생겼지만 착하다'.

examples.ko: 마을 입구에 우람한 느티나무가 서 있어요.
examples.en: A huge zelkova tree stands at the village entrance.
That player has broad, sturdy shoulders.
The mountain is so massive that you feel overwhelmed looking up at it.
Compared with his burly build, his voice was small.
The building rises up grandly.
Before I knew it, my son had become a strapping young man.

explain: 나무, 산, 건물, 체격이 크고 힘 있고 듬직해 보일 때 써요. 감탄하거나 믿음직하다는 좋은 느낌이에요. '우락부락하다'는 거칠어 보이지만 '우람하다'는 무섭다기보다 당당한 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It is used for trees, mountains, buildings or physiques that look big, strong and dependable, usually with admiration. '우락부락하다' looks rough, while '우람하다' feels imposing rather than scary.

en: big baby; super baby; healthy baby

examples.en: My nephew has been a big, healthy baby since birth.
At the checkup I heard that he's a big, healthy baby.
That baby is bigger than others his age, so he's a healthy big baby.
She was born big and healthy, and she drinks formula well.

examples.ko: 요즘은 우량아보다 건강한 성장이 더 중요하대요.
examples.en: They say these days healthy growth matters more than being a big baby.

examples.ko: 우량아 소리를 듣던 아이가 지금은 날씬해요.
examples.en: The kid who used to be called a big baby is slim now.

explain: 또래보다 키와 몸무게가 크고 건강한 아기를 칭찬하듯 부르는 말이에요. 요즘은 크게 자라는 것보다 균형 있게 자라는 것을 중요하게 보는 이야기도 많아요. 아기가 통통하다고 말할 때 '우량아 같아요'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is a word, said almost as praise, for a baby who is bigger and healthier than others of the same age. Today people also talk about balanced growth rather than just size. You can also say '우량아 같아요' about a chubby baby.
